_comment: Facts Brandon supplied that the source document does not state.
The bundled recipe files under KitchenAid/Resources/Recipes are GENERATED by
scripts/import_recipe.py, so hand-editing one is lost the next time its
document is re-imported. Anything he tells us that the document omits is
recorded here instead, keyed by recipe id, and applied on every run.
Keep `why` on every entry. In six months the useful question is not what the
value is but who decided it and whether they are still right.

blueberry-compote.why: Brandon, 2026-11-01: 'they serve approx 4'. The document gives no serving count for any of the three compotes, so the meal planner had nothing to scale by.

turkey-gravy.why: Brandon, 2026-11-08, asked about the two column labels the importer could not place. On 'Fat  1/4 cup (4 tbsp) skimmed turkey fat from the drippings, topped up with UNSALTED butter if short' he said buy NOTHING -- 'it comes from the roast' -- so the line keeps its amount for the cook and is excluded from the shopping list, which is what excludeFromShopping is for. On 'Stock  4 cups UNSALTED turkey or chicken stock, warmed' he chose TURKEY over chicken, so the line is renamed to the thing he buys and 'turkey stock' was added to build_catalogue.py as its own entry. No alias onto chicken stock: the build script fails on an ambiguous lookup, and a name resolving to two purchases makes the pantry match whichever comes first.

_comment: A NOTE-ONLY ENTRY. It sets no field, deliberately -- see why.
Asked how many the turkey serves, Brandon answered that the recipe was
for a roughly 14 lb bird. That is the document's basis, not a serving
count, and the two are not interchangeable: the planner divides by
servings, and inventing a number from a weight would be exactly the kind
of guess this file exists to avoid. So the serving count stays UNSTATED,
its importer warning stays, and nothing here clears it.
He also chose to KEEP 'Pan base' and 'Vegetable bed' flagged rather than
resolve or exclude them, so there is no `lines` block for them on
purpose. Do not 'fix' them: they stay pinned under Needs attention on the
shopping list, which is where he asked for them. Note that Vegetable bed
points at the second component ('leek, garlic, carrots, and celery (see
below)'), whose vegetables ARE listed separately with their own
quantities -- so resolving it to an ingredient would double-count them.
roast-turkey.why: Brandon, 2026-11-08: 'the turkey was for a roughly 14lb turkey', answering a question about servings. Recorded because it is the fact he gave, and kept out of `servings` because it is not one. Scaling a whole roast bird by portions is still an open question -- the document's 8-row weight chart is the honest route, and the Cook screen now has a row picker for it.
